Management:
If broken skin, clean area immediately with soap and water.
If splash to eye/mouth/nose: immediately rinse mouth/nose with water or irrigate eye thoroughly with sodium chloride 0.9% or sterile water.
Assess need for HIV and hepatitis B post-exposure prophylaxis 135.
PROTECT YOURSELF FROM OCCUPATIONAL INFECTION

Reduce TB risk Identify patients with possible TB promptly: • The patient has TB symptoms1. • Separate patients with possible TB from others in the facility. • Educate about cough hygiene and give face mask/tissues to cover mouth/nose to protect others. Diagnose TB rapidly: • Fast track TB workup and start treatment as soon as diagnosed. Screen and test yourself for TB every 6 months: • Screen and test for TB according to your facility policy. If TB test negative, discuss TB preventive treatment (TPT) with your occupational health practitioner.
Manage possible occupational exposure promptly

Reduce risk of respiratory infections • Before managing a patient with possible/confirmed respiratory infection, wear appropriate PPE. • Wash hands with soap and water. • Encourage patient to cover mouth/nose with a tissue when coughing/sneezing, to dispose of used tissues correctly and to wash hands regularly with soap and water. • Advise patient to avoid close contact with others while sick.

Protect yourself Adopt standard precautions with every patient: • Wash hands with soap/water or use alcohol-based cleaner after contact with patient/ body fluids. • Dispose of sharps correctly in sharps bins. Wear protective gear: • Wear gloves when handling blood, body fluids, secretions or non-intact skin. • Wear N95 mask if performing aerosol-generating procedure, if in contact with patient suspected of having respiratory virus or possible/confirmed TB. • Wear surgical mask with a visor or glasses if at risk of splashes. Get vaccinated: • Get vaccinated against hepatitis B (if not yet done) and yearly against influenza. Know your HIV status: • Test for HIV 124. ART and TPT can decrease the risk of TB. • If HIV, you are entitled to work in an area of the facility where exposure to TB is limited.

Protect your facility Clean the facility: • Clean frequently touched surfaces (door handles, telephones, keyboards) daily with soap and water. • Disinfect surfaces contaminated with blood/secretions with 70% alcohol or chlorine-based disinfectant. Ensure adequate ventilation: • Leave windows and doors open when possible and use fans to increase air exchange. Organise waiting areas: • Prevent overcrowding in waiting areas. • Fast track patients with suspected respiratory infections, TB or acute gastroenteritis. Manage sharps safely: • Ensure sharps bins are easily accessible and regularly replaced. Manage infection control in the facility: • Appoint infection control officer to coordinate and monitor infection control policies.
Adopt measures to diminish your risk of occupational infection
1TB symptoms: cough, fever ≥ 2 weeks, unexplained weight loss or drenching night sweats.
